narrative_draft.this_call_happened: Meridian's legal team came back on the BAA question faster than expected: the existing language already covers third-party processing broadly, so it needs a short amendment naming the staging-layer window specifically, not a full renegotiation. Priya confirmed she is satisfied, explicitly echoing Curtis's call-one sign-off, and considers the objection resolved on substance while the amendment is out for signature. Separately, Priya named Dana Whitfield (marketing ops) as the segment owner, closing an open item from the first call. The two of them booked a commercial conversation for the specific date, with Daniel to send a real agenda rather than a status check. The legacy marketing-tool/campaign-authoring question is still unresolved; Priya chased it and marketing wasn't ready to answer.

objections.text: PII/PHI handling at the pre-normalization staging layer — whether the BAA's language actually covers a third-party platform touching PHI at that window
objections.resolution_note: Legal confirmed the existing BAA language covers third-party processing broadly enough to need only a short amendment, and confirmed on Priya's explicit ask that the amendment language names the pre-normalization staging window specifically, not just processing generally. Priya states unambiguous acceptance ('I came away satisfied,' 'resolved on the substance'), the same bar Curtis met in call one. Marcus's technical answer (atomic, encrypted-before-accessible ingestion) is explicitly reaffirmed as unchanged and never in question — this was purely a contracts gap, not a technical one, and both are now closed. Only the signature itself remains outstanding, which is administrative, not substantive.
